content: 1. For patients with severe COVID-19 who require oxygen therapy but do not need mechanical ventilation or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), the use of remdesivir is conditionally recommended. 2. For patients with mild or moderate COVID-19 who are at high risk of progressing to severe disease, remdesivir is conditionally recommended. It should be administered within 7 days of symptom onset. For mild or moderate cases, a 3-day course is recommended. If the condition progresses to severe COVID-19, the duration of remdesivir treatment may be extended as per severe COVID-19 guidelines. 3. For patients with COVID-19 requiring high-flow oxygen or invasive/non-invasive mechanical ventilation, the use of tocilizumab is strongly recommended. 4. For patients with mild COVID-19, the use of tocilizumab is strongly discouraged. 5. No recommendation can be made for or against the use of sarilumab for COVID-19 patients due to insufficient evidence, particularly in the context of South Korea. 6. For patients with severe COVID-19 requiring oxygen therapy but not mechanical ventilation, the use of baricitinib is conditionally recommended. 7. For patients with severe COVID-19 requiring oxygen therapy but not mechanical ventilation, the use of tofacitinib is conditionally recommended. It is suggested to co-administer standard treatments such as antiviral agents and steroids, provided there are no contraindications. 8. No recommendation can be made for or against the use of ruxolitinib for COVID-19 patients due to insufficient evidence on its efficacy and safety. 9. For patients with mild or moderate COVID-19 at high risk of progressing to severe disease who cannot use other antiviral agents, the use of monoclonal antibodies, specifically bebtelovimab, is conditionally recommended. The choice of monoclonal antibody should be guided by the circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants. 10. For patients with severe or critical COVID-19, the use of monoclonal antibodies is not recommended except in clinical trials. 11. During the circulation of Omicron and its subvariants in South Korea, monoclonal antibodies other than bebtelovimab (e.g., amubarvimab/romlusevimab, bamlanivimab, casirivimab/imdevimab, etc.) are not recommended. 12. For individuals unable to mount an adequate immune response after vaccination or those unable to complete vaccination due to severe adverse reactions, the use of tixagevimab/cilgavimab for pre-exposure prophylaxis is conditionally recommended. 13. For patients aged 12 years or older, weighing at least 40 kg, with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 and risk factors for severe disease progression, the use of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) is conditionally recommended. It should be administered within 5 days of symptom onset. 14. For patients aged 18 years or older with mild or moderate COVID-19 at high risk of severe disease progression who cannot use other treatment options, the use of molnupiravir is conditionally recommended. It should be administered within 5 days of symptom onset. 15. For patients with severe or critical COVID-19, the use of steroids is strongly recommended. The recommended dose is 6 mg of dexamethasone daily for up to 10 days. Alternative steroids with equivalent potency may be used. 16. For patients with mild to moderate COVID-19, the use of steroids is strongly discouraged. 17. For early-stage COVID-19, no recommendation can be made for or against the use of inhaled steroids due to insufficient evidence. 18. The use of anakinra (interleukin-1 inhibitor) for COVID-19 patients is discouraged except in clinical trials. 19. No recommendation can be made for or against the use of SARS-CoV-2-specific intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) due to insufficient evidence. 20. For patients with moderate-to-severe COVID-19, the use of convalescent plasma is discouraged. 21. For patients with mild COVID-19, no recommendation can be made for or against the use of convalescent plasma due to insufficient evidence. 22. The use of non-specific IVIG for COVID-19 patients is discouraged except when indicated for treating complications. 23. No recommendation can be made for or against the use of camostat or nafamostat for COVID-19 patients due to insufficient evidence. 24. No recommendation can be made for or against the use of ivermectin for mild, moderate, or severe COVID-19 due to insufficient evidence. 25. The use of interferon for COVID-19 patients is strongly discouraged. 26. The use of favipiravir or umifenovir for COVID-19 patients is discouraged except in clinical trials. 27. No recommendation can be made for or against the use of baloxavir marboxil for COVID-19 patients due to insufficient evidence. 28. For severe COVID-19 patients requiring intensive care, prophylactic-dose heparin is conditionally recommended. For those not requiring intensive care, therapeutic-dose heparin is conditionally recommended unless contraindicated. 29. No recommendation can be made for or against early intubation in COVID-19 patients admitted to the ICU due to insufficient evidence. 30. For patients with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) caused by COVID-19, veno-venous ECMO (vv-ECMO) is suggested if severe hypoxemia persists despite appropriate lung-protective ventilation and prone positioning. 31. For patients with COVID-19 and a PaO2/FiO2 ratio <50 mmHg for more than 3 hours or <80 mmHg for more than 6 hours, vv-ECMO is recommended. 32. For patients with COVID-19 at risk of worsening hypoxemia and no access to ECMO, transfer to a hospital capable of performing ECMO is recommended. 33. For patients aged 70 years or older with advanced frailty and comorbidities, careful consideration of the risks and benefits of ECMO is recommended. 34. For patients with severe ARDS caused by COVID-19, a high-PEEP strategy is suggested over a low-PEEP strategy. 35. For patients with COVID-19 on high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) or non-invasive ventilation, awake prone positioning is suggested. 36. For patients with moderate-to-severe ARDS caused by COVID-19 on invasive mechanical ventilation, prone positioning is strongly recommended. 37. For patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure caused by COVID-19, HFNC therapy is suggested over conventional oxygen therapy. 38. For patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure caused by COVID-19, HFNC therapy or non-invasive mechanical ventilation is suggested based on the patient’s condition and medical staff expertise. 39. For patients with progressive acute hypoxemic respiratory failure caused by COVID-19, prompt initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation is recommended if HFNC therapy fails. 40. For patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure caused by COVID-19, HFNC therapy may be considered as an alternative to invasive mechanical ventilation when life-sustaining treatments are discontinued. 41. For the initial treatment of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), IVIG combined with steroids is suggested over IVIG or steroids alone. 42. For MIS-C patients unresponsive to IVIG and/or steroids, other immunomodulators (e.g., interleukin-1 inhibitors, interleukin-6 inhibitors, TNF-α inhibitors) are suggested. 43. Low-dose aspirin is suggested to prevent thrombosis in MIS-C patients. 44. For pediatric patients aged 28 days or older and weighing at least 3 kg with severe COVID-19 requiring supplemental oxygen, remdesivir is suggested. A 5-day course is recommended, even if the patient progresses to requiring mechanical ventilation or ECMO. 45. For pediatric patients aged 12 years or older and weighing at least 40 kg with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 at high risk of severe disease progression, remdesivir is suggested within 7 days of symptom onset. A 3-day course is recommended, with extension to 5 days if the condition worsens. 46. For pediatric patients with severe-to-critical COVID-19 requiring supplemental oxygen, steroids (dexamethasone) are suggested. 47. For pediatric patients aged 2 years or older with severe or critical COVID-19, tocilizumab in addition to steroids is considered. 48. For pediatric patients aged 12 years or older and weighing at least 40 kg with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 at high risk of severe disease progression, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is suggested within 5 days of symptom onset. 49. The use of mechanical CPR devices is suggested for cardiac arrest in COVID-19 patients to reduce aerosol transmission risk. 50. The rapid antigen test (RAT) is recommended alongside PCR testing for enhanced diagnostic accuracy. 51. RAT alone is generally not recommended for suspected COVID-19 cases but may be used during high prevalence when PCR testing is limited. 52. Contrast-enhanced chest CT is suggested for patients with suspected pulmonary embolism due to elevated D-dimer levels and symptoms such as dyspnea, hypoxia, and chest pain. 53. Chest X-ray follow-ups are suggested during and after COVID-19 treatment. 54. Portable personal negative pressure isolation chambers (NPIC) are suggested for chest CT scans in high-risk COVID-19 patients to prevent transmission.
